ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A person is rowing a boat upstream. When the boat passes under a small bridge, a small wooden block falls into the river from the boat. However, the person only realizes this when the boat has traveled some distance upstream. The person immediately turns around and starts rowing downstream to catch up with the wooden block. After rowing downstream for 1 hour, the person catches up with the wooden block and finds that it is 5400 meters away from the small bridge. Assume that the speed of the boat in still water is the same when rowing upstream and downstream.

1. What is the flow velocity of the river?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A person is rowing a boat upstream. When the boat passes under a small bridge, a small wooden block falls into the river from the boat. However, the person only realizes this when the boat has traveled some distance upstream. The person immediately turns around and starts rowing downstream to catch up with the wooden block. After rowing downstream for 1 hour, the person catches up with the wooden block and finds that it is 5400 meters away from the small bridge. Assume that the speed of the boat in still water is the same when rowing upstream and downstream. What is the flow velocity of the river?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Use the river-current reference frame. In this frame, the wooden block is at rest at the point where it fell into the water, while the boat moves relative to the water with its still-water speed. Let the time the person continues rowing upstream before noticing the block is missing be t. Since the boat rows upstream and then downstream with the same speed relative to the water, the time needed to return to the stationary block in this frame is also t. The downstream rowing time is given as 1 hour, so t = 1 hour. Therefore, the wooden block has drifted in the bridge/ground frame for a total time of 1 hour + 1 hour = 2 hours. It is then 5400 m from the bridge, so the river flow speed is 5400 m / 2 h = 2700 m/h = 2700/3600 m/s = 0.75 m/s.

At the turn, the boat is at position −(u−v)t relative to the bridge, while the block is at vt. During the next 1 hour, the boat moves downstream with ground speed u+v, so its catch position is −(u−v)t + (u+v). The block’s position then is v(t+1). Equate positions: −(u−v)t + (u+v) = v(t+1). Simplifying gives u(1−t)=0, hence t = 1 hour. The catch point is 5400 m from the bridge, equal to the block’s drift v(t+1) = 2v hours, so v = 5400 m / 2 h = 0.75 m/s.

The wooden block simply drifts downstream with the river, so its position then is x_block = vt. After the rower turns around, the boat rows downstream for 1 hour with ground speed u + v, so its catch-up position is x_boat = -(u - v)t + (u + v).
